`tests/testthat/test-scenario-exposure-witness.R`, committed evidence under

## 1. Mandate

Pillar 3's tenth decision-record scenario. The scoping pass selected the
exported two-group exposure-differentiation face `ms_exposure_test()`
(`R/ms-embed.R`, the per-signature Wilcoxon with BH family correction and
the alpha gate) -- a face whose unit suite speaks the machinery (the
BH-vs-correction identity, the all-tied NA face, the error paths) but
never renders the shipped decision over a planted differential matrix:
the full-family semantics -- pass bits, flip vectors across family sizes,
the NA face, the input-law set -- had never been committed as a decision
record by any lane. Everything here is closed-form by construction: the
plant is pure arithmetic, the executed path touches no RNG and no network,
and there is no seed to pin. The face is called FRESH per arm; zero
global state, no injected-manifest seam.

## 2. The plant and the six arms

The plant is six signature legs over 24 samples in two 12-sample groups
(A/B), every leg closed-form arithmetic from the base ramp
`v = (0..11)/12` -- D3 law: synthetic `9.x/2.x` leg labels and arithmetic
bytes only, zero COSMIC numeric matrices, zero downloads. The six arms,
every one driven through the EXPORTED face alone (no hand-rolled
rank-sum test and no hand-rolled family correction is invoked anywhere in
the lane):

- **designed** -- legs `9.4` (B-high) and `2.6` (A-high) pass `pass_bh`
  at the frozen alpha 0.05; the wilcoxon statistic, both medians and both
  p-columns are committed per leg from the live face.
- **decoy** -- leg `9.1` mirrors its second half: the SAME distribution,
  not element-wise equal (it escapes the NA face), speaks `p = 1`, and
  stays negative.
- **tied/NA face** -- leg `2.2`: `statistic`/`p_raw`/`p_bh` all NA (NOT a
  fabricated p), `pass_bh` FALSE, and the medians are still spoken.
- **borderline** -- leg `9.8` at the frozen delta 0.18: a rank-plateau
  was measured across the tuning sweep (deltas 0.10-0.16 share one p,
  0.18-0.20 the next), and 0.18 was chosen so the leg fails the frozen
  alpha while the ladder admits it at alpha 0.2 -- an observed
  bracketing witness.
- **BH ladder** -- family rosters {six legs} x {five legs (the family-size
  leg dropped)} across alphas {0.001, 0.05, 0.2}: the committed flip
  vector per rung. The designed legs never flip across the meaningful
  range; the borderline leg's admission at 0.2 is a COMMITTED OBSERVED
  fact, and the fold-back law (`p_bh >= p_raw`, cap at 1) is censused at
  every rung.
- **input-law set** -- seven probes (three-group design, alphas 0/1/2,
  groups-length mismatch, character matrix, list groups): every one
  ABORTS with class `msuiter_error_input` and the committed clause,
  verbatim -- including the two-group law's caller's-decision clause.

The label-fallback law (NULL rownames -> `sig1..sigk`) and the
MsSignature-equivalence arm (an object input built the sanctioned way --
`ms_catalog()` -> `msuiter_catalog_summary()` so the channel hash stays
DERIVED, never hand-forged -- is `all.equal` to the raw-matrix input)
close the face.

## 3. The measured laws this scenario commits

- **The family-size modulation record.** Dropping the fifth passing leg
  re-weights the BH ladder: the borderline leg's corrected p moves from
  0.1488 (six-leg family) to 0.1587 (five-leg family) -- MORE
  conservative with a SMALLER family, because the passing rank beneath it
  disappeared -- while still failing 0.05 on both sides. The flip vectors
  are committed per rung: six-leg family passes {9.4, 2.6, 2.9} at 0.05
  and gains 9.8 at 0.2; five-leg family passes {9.4, 2.6} at 0.05.
  Nothing here is derived from BH theory -- these are OBSERVED facts about
  the shipped face, spoken by measurement.
- **The NA face speaks zero fabrications.** Across all 33 ladder rungs
  the tied leg is the only NA, it never carries a pass, and the
  no-fabrication rail (`pass == 1 & is.na(p_bh)` counts zero) holds
  everywhere.
- **Instrument failures caught fail-closed, twice more.** (i) The
  witness-finiteness census refused the first commit: this base renders
  `as.character(NA)` as a REAL `NA` character, not the string `"NA"`, so
  the intended "NA" token entered the degenerates witness as a poisoned
  cell and the pre-write census (correctly) denied the commit -- fixed by
  routing the float render through `paste0`, which speaks the literal.
  (ii) The zero-warning pristineness law then exposed a census trap: 18
  coercion warnings inside `expect_equal` calls were being double-counted
  as results (a first green printed nb=179 where the literal expect count
  is 161 -- 179 = 161 + 18 warns); the readers now take `na.strings = ""`
  and a reserved-token converter maps `"NA"` back to a real NA BEFORE any
  coercion. The final green is 161/161 with zero warnings -- a count the
  file itself can be audited against. Both events are
  OBSERVATION-instrument failures caught by the project's own laws before
  any verdict was committed, never verdict failures.

## 4. Hard rails and postures

The hard rails: the committed pass bits and statistic vector; the decoy's
`p = 1` and finite statistic; the tied leg's triple-NA with spoken
medians; the six committed flip vectors; the fold-back and cap laws at
every rung; the seven input-law classes and clauses; the label fallback;
the MsSignature equivalence; the plant-checksum dual-kernel identity (the
canonical pure-R SHA-256 and the `digest` accelerator agree on the
plant's bytes); and the pre-write witness-finiteness census. Postures:
DECISION RECORD only -- no calibration, no coverage claim, no intervals,
no bootstrap, no conformal framing (the declined words are spoken by the
runner itself); the D11 float posture is honored in full -- the witness
byte-freezes integer and label verdicts only, the float columns are
re-derived LIVE through the same face at tolerance, never sealed as
cross-platform bytes; the pillar-2 namespace-reach idiom is banned in the
law file and grepped away.
